questions.question: According to Bohr’s model of the atom, electrons in an atom:

options.text: are stationary in the atom and emit energy when struck by photons
revolve around the nucleus in elliptical orbits and emit energy continuously
are embedded in a positively charged sphere like plums in a pudding
revolve in fixed circular orbits and do not radiate energy while in these orbits

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**revolve in fixed circular orbits and do not radiate energy while in these orbits**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bohr's atomic model** proposed that **electrons revolve around the nucleus in fixed circular orbits**, also known as energy levels or shells. These orbits are quantized, meaning electrons can only occupy specific, defined levels of energy.
 
• While in these fixed orbits, **electrons do not emit or lose energy**, contradicting classical electromagnetic theory, which suggests that accelerating charges (like electrons) should radiate energy.
 
• Electrons can move between energy levels by **absorbing or emitting discrete amounts of energy**, called quanta. The energy change corresponds to the difference in energy between the two levels.
 
• Bohr introduced the **concept of quantization**, which explains why atoms exhibit specific spectral lines. These lines are produced when electrons transition between energy levels.
 
• This model successfully explained the **hydrogen atom's spectral lines** but was later found inadequate for more complex atoms and was succeeded by quantum mechanics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Features of Bohr's Model:**

 
 
• Electrons are confined to fixed orbits or shells around the nucleus, and each orbit corresponds to a specific energy level.
 
• These orbits are stable, and electrons in these orbits do not radiate energy, addressing the instability predicted by Rutherford's model.
 
• The energy of an electron depends on the orbit it occupies, with **lower energy closer to the nucleus** and **higher energy farther away**.
 
• The model introduced the idea of **quantized angular momentum**, with electrons having angular momentum equal to an integer multiple of h/2π (where h is Planck's constant).
 
 
 
• **Limitations of Bohr's Model:**
 
 
• The model could only accurately explain the spectrum of hydrogen and hydrogen-like ions (single-electron systems) but failed for multi-electron atoms.
 
• It could not explain the finer details of spectral lines, such as splitting due to the Zeeman effect or Stark effect.
 
• Bohr's model was later replaced by the more comprehensive **quantum mechanical model** of the atom, which incorporates wave-particle duality and probabilistic electron behavior.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Atomic Models:**
 
 
• **Thomson's Model:** Proposed that electrons are embedded in a positively charged sphere, like plums in a pudding. This model was incorrect as it could not explain atomic stability.
 
• **Rutherford's Model:** Suggested that electrons revolve around a dense, positively charged nucleus. However, it failed to explain why electrons do not spiral into the nucleus due to energy radiation.
 
• **Quantum Mechanical Model:** This modern model uses **Schrödinger's wave equation** and describes electrons as existing in probability clouds (orbitals) rather than fixed orbits.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Bohr's Model:**
 
 
• Explained the **Rydberg formula** for the spectral emission lines of the hydrogen atom.
 
• Provided a foundation for understanding atomic structure and behavior, paving the way for quantum mechanics.
 
• Helped in the calculation of ionization energy and excitation energy for hydrogen-like atoms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Statement Analysis:**

 
 
• **Option 1:** Incorrect. Electrons are not stationary and do not emit energy upon being struck by photons.
 
• **Option 2:** Incorrect. Bohr's model describes electrons in circular, not elliptical orbits, and they do not emit energy continuously.
 
• **Option 3:** Incorrect. This is Thomson's "plum pudding" model, which was disproven by Rutherford's gold foil experiment.
 
• **Option 4:** Correct. Electrons revolve in fixed circular orbits and do not radiate energy while in these orbits, as described by Bohr's model.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:** Bohr's model was proposed in **1913**, combining classical mechanics and early quantum theory.
 
• **Significance:** The model laid the groundwork for modern atomic theory and quantum mechanics, revolutionizing our understanding of atomic and subatomic behavior.

questions.question: Which of the following non-metals is found liquid at room temperature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bromine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bromine** is the only non-metal that exists as a liquid at room temperature (approximately 25°C).
 
• It has a **melting point of -7.2°C** and a **boiling point of 58.8°C**, which means it remains in the liquid state under standard room conditions.
 
• **Bromine** is a reddish-brown liquid with a pungent odor and is highly volatile, forming toxic fumes.
 
• It belongs to the **halogen group (Group 17)** of the periodic table, which also includes fluorine, chlorine, iodine, and astatine.
 
• Bromine is widely used in industries for the production of **flame retardants, pesticides, and dyes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Iodine**:

 
 
• Iodine is a solid at room temperature and has a melting point of 113.7°C and a boiling point of 184.3°C.
 
• It is primarily used in **iodized salt** and as an antiseptic in medicines.
 
• Iodine is a member of the halogen group and exists in a crystalline form with a metallic luster.
 
 
 
• **Nitrogen**:
 
 
• Nitrogen is a gas at room temperature with a boiling point of -195.8°C and a melting point of -210°C.
 
• It makes up approximately **78% of Earth's atmosphere** and is essential for the formation of amino acids and proteins in living organisms.
 
• Nitrogen is used industrially in the production of fertilizers, explosives, and as a cryogenic agent.
 
 
 
• **Phosphorus**:
 
 
• Phosphorus exists in several allotropes, with **white phosphorus** and **red phosphorus** being the most common.
 
• At room temperature, phosphorus is a solid with a melting point of 44.1°C (white phosphorus).
 
• It is widely used in the production of fertilizers, explosives, and matches.
 
 
 
• **Bromine**:
 
 
• Bromine is a unique non-metallic element because it is a liquid at room temperature.
 
• Its applications include **fire retardants, water treatment chemicals, and photographic films.**
 
• Bromine is toxic and corrosive, requiring careful handling and storage.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Unique Properties of Bromine:**

 
 
• Bromine's liquid state at room temperature is a result of its moderate intermolecular forces, specifically **van der Waals forces.**
 
• It is highly reactive and forms compounds with a wide range of elements.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Halogens:**
 
 
• Other halogens such as chlorine and fluorine are gases at room temperature, while iodine and astatine are solids.
 
• This variability in physical states among halogens is due to differences in atomic mass and intermolecular forces.
 
 
 
• **Safety Precautions:**
 
 
• Bromine is highly toxic and can cause severe burns upon contact with the skin.
 
• Proper ventilation, protective clothing, and equipment are essential when handling bromine.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of human male chromosome is mismatched in size?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sex chromosomes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sex chromosomes** in human males consist of one **X chromosome** and one **Y chromosome**. These chromosomes are mismatched in size, with the X chromosome being significantly larger than the Y chromosome.
 
• The **X chromosome** contains approximately 155 million base pairs and hosts several hundred genes, while the **Y chromosome** is much smaller, with only about 58 million base pairs and fewer than 80 genes.
 
• This size difference is due to the evolutionary loss of genetic material on the Y chromosome over time, making it much smaller and gene-poor compared to the X chromosome.
 
• In contrast, autosomes are paired chromosomes that are generally similar in size and genetic content, making them matched pairs.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is "Sex chromosomes."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chromosomes:**

 
 
• Humans have **46 chromosomes**, organized into 23 pairs. These include 22 pairs of autosomes and 1 pair of sex chromosomes.
 
• **Autosomes:** These are non-sex chromosomes and are numbered from 1 to 22 based on size, with chromosome 1 being the largest.
 
• **Sex chromosomes:** In males, the sex chromosome pair is **XY**, and in females, it is **XX**. The Y chromosome determines male sex characteristics.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Sex Chromosomes:**
 
 
• The **X chromosome** plays a vital role in both sexes, as it carries genes related to essential functions such as vision, immunity, and reproduction.
 
• The **Y chromosome** carries genes like **SRY (Sex-determining Region Y)**, which is crucial for the development of male gonads (testes).
 
 
 
• **Autosomal Chromosomes:**
 
 
• These chromosomes contain genes responsible for most of the body's structures and functions, such as metabolic processes, growth, and immunity.
 
• Autosomal pairs are homologous, meaning both chromosomes in a pair are similar in size and gene content.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Chromosome Pairs:**
 
 
• The **first pair of autosomes** is the largest, while the **twentieth pair** and other smaller autosomal pairs are similar in size.
 
• Unlike autosomes, sex chromosomes differ significantly, with the Y chromosome being much smaller than the X chromosome.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Genetic Disorders Related to Sex Chromosomes:**

 
 
• **Turner Syndrome:** Occurs in females who have only one X chromosome (45, X0).
 
• **Klinefelter Syndrome:** A condition in males with an extra X chromosome (47, XXY).
 
• **Y-linked disorders:** Rare disorders caused by mutations in genes present on the Y chromosome.
 
 
 
• **Chromosomal Studies:**
 
 
• Chromosome analysis is essential for diagnosing genetic conditions and understanding evolutionary biology.
 
• Techniques like **karyotyping** and **fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH)** are used for studying chromosomes.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT present in animal cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chloroplast**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chloroplasts** are **absent in animal cells**. These organelles are specific to plant cells and some algae, where they are responsible for **photosynthesis**, a process that converts light energy into chemical energy stored as glucose.
 
• Animal cells do not perform photosynthesis as they obtain energy by consuming organic matter rather than producing it. *Hence, chloroplasts are absent in animal cells.*
 
• **Nucleus**, **plasma membrane**, and **cytoplasm** are present in both animal and plant cells. These are essential components for cellular function. *Hence, these options are incorrect.*
 
• The **nucleus** houses the genetic material (DNA) and controls cellular activities, making it an indispensable organelle in all eukaryotic cells.
 
• The **plasma membrane**, also known as the cell membrane, surrounds the cell, providing structural support, protection, and regulating the movement of substances in and out of the cell.
 
• The **cytoplasm** is the jelly-like substance filling the cell, where various metabolic processes and organelle activities take place. It is present in all cell types.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chloroplast:**

 
 
• Chloroplasts are double-membrane-bound organelles found in plant cells and certain protists like algae.
 
• They contain the pigment **chlorophyll**, which captures light energy for photosynthesis.
 
• Chloroplasts have their own DNA and ribosomes, enabling them to produce some of their own proteins.
 
• They are responsible for converting light energy into glucose and oxygen, which are essential for the survival of plants and indirectly for all living organisms.
 
 
 
• **Nucleus:**
 
 
• The nucleus is a membrane-bound organelle present in all eukaryotic cells.
 
• It contains the cell's genetic material in the form of DNA, organized into chromosomes.
 
• It regulates essential cellular functions such as growth, metabolism, protein synthesis, and cell division.
 
 
 
• **Plasma Membrane:**
 
 
• The plasma membrane is a semi-permeable structure made of a phospholipid bilayer embedded with proteins.
 
• It regulates the movement of molecules such as nutrients, waste, and ions in and out of the cell.
 
• In animal cells, it is the outermost layer, whereas in plant cells, it is located beneath the cell wall.
 
 
 
• **Cytoplasm:**
 
 
• The cytoplasm is the gel-like substance enclosed within the cell membrane.
 
• It contains organelles such as mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, and Golgi apparatus, as well as cytosol, a fluid component.
 
• It is the site of various cellular processes, including glycolysis and intracellular transport.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Plant vs. Animal Cells:**

 
 
• Plant cells have a rigid cell wall, chloroplasts, and a large central vacuole, which are absent in animal cells.
 
• Animal cells have centrioles and lysosomes, which are not typically found in plant cells.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis:**
 
 
• This process occurs in the chloroplasts of plant cells, where light energy is converted into chemical energy.
 
• The equation for photosynthesis is: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.
 
 
 
• **Endosymbiotic Theory:**
 
 
• Chloroplasts and mitochondria are believed to have originated from free-living prokaryotes through endosymbiosis.
 
• This theory is supported by the presence of their own DNA and double membranes.

questions.question: Which of the following is the common name for ethanol (C₂H₅OH) ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ethyl alcohol**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ethanol**, with the chemical formula **C₂H₅OH**, is commonly known as **Ethyl alcohol**. It is a simple alcohol consisting of a two-carbon chain with a hydroxyl group (-OH).
 
• **Ethyl alcohol** is widely used in **alcoholic beverages** due to its psychoactive properties. It is the primary ingredient responsible for intoxication in such drinks.
 
• The term **ethyl alcohol** is derived from the ethyl group (C₂H₅), which is a functional group present in ethanol's structure.
 
• Ethanol is a versatile compound with extensive applications, including its use as a **solvent in industries**, a **fuel additive** (bioethanol), and a **disinfectant** in medical applications.
 
• Other alcohols like **methyl alcohol** (methanol), **butyl alcohol**, and **isopropyl alcohol** have distinct chemical structures and uses, making them different from ethanol.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Methyl alcohol (Methanol):**

 
 
• Its chemical formula is **CH₃OH**.
 
• It is also known as **wood alcohol** and is primarily used as a solvent, antifreeze, or fuel.
 
• Methanol is highly toxic and can cause blindness or death if ingested.
 
 
 
• **Butyl alcohol:**
 
 
• Its chemical formula is **C₄H₉OH**.
 
• This alcohol has several isomers and is often used as an industrial solvent or in the production of plastics and coatings.
 
 
 
• **Isopropyl alcohol:**
 
 
• Its chemical formula is **C₃H₈O**.
 
• Also known as **rubbing alcohol**, it is commonly used as a disinfectant and cleaning agent.
 
• It is not suitable for consumption and can be toxic if ingested.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Ethanol:**
 
 
• As a fuel additive, ethanol is mixed with gasoline to create **gasohol**, helping to reduce air pollution.
 
• In the pharmaceutical industry, ethanol is used as a **solvent** for medicinal formulations.
 
• It is also employed in the production of perfumes, cosmetics, and other personal care products.
 
 
 
• **Production of Ethanol:**
 
 
• Ethanol is commonly produced by the **fermentation of sugars** found in crops like corn, sugarcane, and wheat.
 
• Industrially, it can also be synthesized through the **hydration of ethylene**.

questions.question: A light is travelling from a denser medium A to a rarer medium B. What will be the unit of refractive index of medium B with respect to medium A?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**No unit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **refractive index** is a ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to the speed of light in the given medium. It is expressed as:

 Refractive Index (n) = Speed of Light in Vacuum / Speed of Light in Medium.
 
• Since it is a ratio of two quantities with the same units (speed), the resulting value is **dimensionless**, meaning it has **no unit**.
 
• In the given scenario, light travels from a denser medium A to a rarer medium B. The refractive index of medium B with respect to medium A is represented as:

 nBA = Speed of Light in Medium A / Speed of Light in Medium B.
 
• The refractive index simply compares how much light slows down in one medium compared to another and does not involve any physical units.
 
• **Hence, the refractive index of medium B with respect to medium A is unitless.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Refractive Index:**

 
 
• The refractive index is a fundamental property of transparent materials and determines the bending of light (refraction) when passing from one medium to another.
 
• A higher refractive index indicates that light travels slower in the medium, while a lower refractive index means light travels faster.
 
• Example: The refractive index of water is approximately 1.33, meaning light travels 1.33 times slower in water compared to a vacuum.
 
 
 
• **Snell's Law:**
 
 
• Snell's Law governs the relationship between the angles of incidence and refraction when light passes between two media with different refractive indices.
 
• It is expressed as: n₁sinθ₁ = n₂sinθ₂, where n₁ and n₂ are the refractive indices of the two media, and θ₁ and θ₂ are the angles of incidence and refraction, respectively.
 
 
 
• **Relative Refractive Index:**
 
 
• The relative refractive index compares the refractive indices of two media, such as medium A and medium B, and is given by nBA = nB/nA.
 
• This value helps determine the direction and extent of light bending when transitioning between the two media.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Refractive Index:**
 
 
• Used in designing lenses for optical instruments like cameras, microscopes, and telescopes.
 
• Helps in identifying materials based on their optical properties, such as gemstones or liquids.
 
• Plays a crucial role in fiber optics and telecommunications for efficient signal transmission.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Absolute Refractive Index:** This is the refractive index of a medium with respect to a vacuum and is always greater than or equal to 1.
 
• **Critical Angle:** The angle of incidence in the denser medium at which the angle of refraction becomes 90° in the rarer medium.
 
• **Total Internal Reflection:** When light traveling from a denser to a rarer medium hits the interface at an angle greater than the critical angle, it gets completely reflected back into the denser medium.
 
• **Optical Density:** A medium with a higher refractive index is considered optically denser than one with a lower refractive index, irrespective of its physical density.

questions.question: A train is moving along a straight track with a speed of 54 km/hr. It stops after traveling 150 m. The magnitude of its acceleration is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.75 m/s²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Initial speed of the train:** The train is moving at a speed of **54 km/hr**. Converting this into meters per second: *54 km/hr = (54 × 1000) / (60 × 60) = 15 m/s*. Hence, the initial velocity is **15 m/s**.
 
• **Final speed of the train:** The train stops after traveling 150 meters. Therefore, its final velocity is **0 m/s**.
 
• **Displacement:** The train travels a distance of **150 meters**, which is the displacement during deceleration.
 
• **Formula used:** To calculate the acceleration, we use the kinematic equation: *v² = u² + 2as*, where **v** is the final velocity, **u** is the initial velocity, **a** is the acceleration, and **s** is the displacement.
 
• **Calculation:** Substituting the values: *0² = 15² + 2 × a × 150*. Simplifying: *0 = 225 + 300a*. Solving for **a**: *a = -225 / 300 = -0.75 m/s²*. The negative sign indicates deceleration. The magnitude of acceleration is **0.75 m/s²**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Acceleration Definition:** Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with respect to time. It is measured in meters per second squared (m/s²). A negative acceleration indicates deceleration or slowing down.
 
• **Kinematic Equations:** These equations are used to solve problems in motion under uniform acceleration. The three main equations are:
 
 
• *v = u + at*
 
• *s = ut + 0.5at²*
 
• *v² = u² + 2as*
 
 
 
• **Units of Speed and Acceleration:** Speed is measured in meters per second (m/s), and acceleration is measured in meters per second squared (m/s²). Conversions between units, such as km/hr to m/s, are crucial in physics calculations.
 
• **Real-life Applications of Deceleration:** Deceleration calculations are essential in designing brakes for vehicles, analyzing train stopping distances, and ensuring safety in transportation systems.
 
• **Importance of Negative Acceleration:** Negative acceleration helps in understanding the rate at which an object slows down. It is particularly useful in analyzing motion dynamics in braking systems and collision scenarios.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Uniform Acceleration:** This occurs when the acceleration of an object remains constant over time. Examples include free fall motion under gravity and vehicles decelerating uniformly.
 
• **Kinetic Energy in Motion:** The train's motion involves kinetic energy, calculated using the formula *KE = 0.5mv²*, where **m** is mass and **v** is velocity. As the train decelerates, its kinetic energy decreases.
 
• **Stopping Distance:** The distance required for a train or vehicle to come to a complete stop depends on initial velocity, acceleration (or deceleration), and frictional forces.
 
• **Safety Measures:** Accurate calculations of deceleration are crucial in designing effective braking systems and ensuring passenger safety during sudden stops.
 
• **Applications in Physics:** Understanding motion under uniform acceleration forms the foundation of classical mechanics and is widely applied in engineering, transportation, and safety design.

questions.question: A car driver uses a concave mirror as a shaving mirror at home. If his face is kept close to the mirror, how will the image formed be?

options.text: Real, inverted, and larger than the face
Real, inverted, and smaller than the face

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Virtual, erect, and magnified**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Concave mirrors** are spherical mirrors with a reflecting surface that curves inward. They are capable of forming both real and virtual images based on the object's position relative to the mirror's focal point.
 
• When a person's face is placed **close to a concave mirror** (i.e., within its focal length), the mirror produces a **virtual, erect, and magnified image**. This happens because the reflected rays appear to diverge, and the image is formed on the same side as the object.
 
• For a concave mirror, the nature of the image depends on the **object's position**:
 
 
• When the object is beyond the center of curvature, the image is real, inverted, and smaller.
 
• When the object is at the focal point, no image is formed as the reflected rays are parallel.
 
• When the object is within the focal length, as in the case of shaving mirrors, the image is virtual, erect, and magnified.
 
 
 
• Shaving mirrors are typically designed to have a **short focal length**, ensuring that the face is within the focal length of the mirror to produce a magnified image. This feature allows the user to see a clear and enlarged reflection of their face for precise grooming.
 
• **Magnification** occurs because the reflected rays diverge as if they are originating from a point behind the mirror, creating a larger virtual image.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Uses of Concave Mirrors:**

 
 
• In **shaving mirrors** to produce a magnified and clear image of the face.
 
• In **telescopes** to gather and focus light from distant objects.
 
• In **dentistry**, dentists use concave mirrors to view an enlarged image of teeth for better diagnosis.
 
• In **headlights and flashlights**, concave mirrors are used to focus light into a beam.
 
 
 
• **Key Characteristics of Concave Mirrors:**
 
 
• They have a **real focus** (light rays converge at the focal point).
 
• Their reflective surface is on the inner side of the spherical shape.
 
• The type of image they form depends on the **object's position** relative to the focal point and center of curvature.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Convex Mirrors:**
 
 
• **Concave mirrors** can form real and virtual images, while **convex mirrors** always produce virtual, erect, and diminished images.
 
• Convex mirrors are used as **rear-view mirrors** in vehicles because they provide a wide field of view.
 
 
 
• **Image Formation by Concave Mirrors:**
 
 
• Beyond the center of curvature: Real, inverted, and smaller than the object.
 
• At the center of curvature: Real, inverted, and the same size as the object.
 
• Between the center of curvature and the focal point: Real, inverted, and magnified.
 
• At the focal point: No image is formed (rays are parallel).
 
• Within the focal length: Virtual, erect, and magnified.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• Concave mirrors are widely used in optical instruments, scientific equipment, and daily-use tools like shaving mirrors and makeup mirrors.
 
• They are also used in solar devices, such as **solar cookers**, to focus sunlight for heating purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Biodegradable waste** refers to materials that can be broken down by microorganisms such as bacteria and fungi into simpler organic forms and natural elements. Items such as **wooden pencil shavings** fall under this category as they are derived from wood, which is a natural and organic material.
 
• **Glass bottles** are not biodegradable as they are made of inorganic materials that do not decompose naturally. Instead, they require recycling processes. *Hence, option 1 is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Biodegradable Materials:**

 
 
• Include organic materials such as **food scraps, paper, leaves, wood, and cotton**.
 
• Break down naturally through the action of microorganisms, returning nutrients to the soil.
 
• Examples: Vegetable peels, wood shavings, paper products, and garden waste.

• Include synthetic and inorganic materials such as **plastic, glass, and metal**.
 
• Do not decompose naturally and can persist in the environment for decades or centuries.
 
• Examples: Plastic bags, glass bottles, aluminum cans, and synthetic fibers.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• Biodegradable waste, when properly composted, can improve soil quality and reduce landfill waste.
 
• Non-biodegradable waste contributes to **pollution, habitat destruction, and health hazards**.
 
 
 
• **Composting:**
 
 
• A process of recycling organic waste into nutrient-rich fertilizer for plants.
 
• Requires biodegradable materials like **fruit peels, yard trimmings, and wooden shavings.**
 
 
 
• **Recycling:**
 
 
• Non-biodegradable materials like glass and aluminum can be recycled to reduce environmental impact.
 
• Recycling processes conserve resources and reduce the production of waste.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Government Initiatives:**

 
 
• Programs like **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan** emphasize waste segregation into biodegradable and non-biodegradable categories.
 
• Encouragement of **composting and recycling** to manage biodegradable and non-biodegradable waste effectively.
 
 
 
• **Segregation at Source:**
 
 
• Segregating waste at the source is crucial for effective waste management and environmental protection.
 
• Biodegradable waste can be composted, while non-biodegradable waste should be sent for recycling or proper disposal.
 
 
 
• **Educational Importance:**
 
 
• Schools and institutions play a key role in educating students about the importance of waste segregation and sustainability.
 
• Activities like campus cleaning help inculcate responsibility and awareness in students.

questions.question: The generation of heat in a conductor due to electric current is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Joule’s heating**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Joule’s heating**, also known as **ohmic heating** or **resistive heating**, occurs when an electric current passes through a conductor, producing heat due to the resistance of the material.
 
• The heat generated in the conductor is governed by **Joule’s Law**, which states that the heat produced is directly proportional to the square of the current (*I*), the resistance (*R*), and the time (*t*) for which the current flows: *H = I²Rt*.
 
• Joule’s heating effect is utilized in various devices such as **electric heaters**, **toasters**, **electric kettles**, and **incandescent bulbs**.
 
• The phenomenon is a result of collisions between electrons (carrying current) and the lattice ions in the conductor, which convert the electrical energy into thermal energy.
 
• This effect is not ideal for transmission of electricity over long distances as it leads to **energy loss** in the form of heat, thus necessitating efficient electrical systems to minimize Joule’s heating.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electrolysis:**

 
 
• Electrolysis is a chemical process where **electric current causes the decomposition** of a compound in a liquid solution or molten state, typically used in the extraction or purification of metals.
 
• An example is the **electrolysis of water**, which splits water molecules into **hydrogen** and **oxygen gases**.
 
• It is fundamentally different from Joule’s heating as it involves chemical changes rather than heat generation.
 
 
 
• **Ohm’s Law:**
 
 
• Ohm’s Law defines the relationship between voltage (*V*), current (*I*), and resistance (*R*) in an electrical circuit: *V = IR*.
 
• It does not directly explain the generation of heat, but it helps in calculating the current or resistance, which can then be used in **Joule’s heating formula**.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetic Induction:**
 
 
• This phenomenon occurs when an electric current is generated in a conductor due to a changing magnetic field.
 
• It is the principle behind devices like **generators** and **transformers** and does not involve the generation of heat like Joule’s heating.
 
• Discovered by **Michael Faraday** in **1831**, electromagnetic induction is central to modern power generation systems.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Joule’s Heating:**
 
 
• It is widely used in heating devices such as **electric irons**, **room heaters**, and **electric stoves**.
 
• It plays a role in the functioning of **fuses**, where excessive current causes heating and breaks the circuit.
 
• Joule’s heating is also utilized in **thermistors** and **temperature-dependent resistors** for various applications.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Energy Loss in Transmission:**

 
 
• Joule’s heating leads to significant **energy loss** during the transmission of electricity over long distances, which is why **high voltage transmission** is preferred to minimize current and reduce losses.
 
 
 
• **Practical Limitations:**
 
 
• Excessive Joule’s heating can damage electrical components and circuits, necessitating the use of **cooling systems** and **efficient designs**.
 
 
 
• **Discovery:**
 
 
• Joule’s heating was first described by **James Prescott Joule** in the **1840s**, laying the foundation for thermodynamics and modern electrical engineering.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly explains the continuous movement of particles of matter?

options.text: Particles of matter are too heavy to move.
Particles of matter are stationary unless force is applied.
Particles of matter are continuously moving due to their kinetic energy.
Particles of matter move only in gases and not in solids or liquids.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Particles of matter are continuously moving due to their kinetic energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Particles of matter possess kinetic energy**, which is the energy due to their motion. This intrinsic property ensures that particles remain in continuous motion.
 
• The **movement of particles** occurs in all states of matter—solids, liquids, and gases—but varies depending on the state. For example, particles in gases move more freely than in solids or liquids.
 
• **Brownian motion**, an observable phenomenon, demonstrates the continuous movement of particles. It can be seen when particles suspended in a fluid exhibit random motion.
 
• The kinetic energy of particles is directly related to temperature. As temperature increases, the kinetic energy of the particles increases, causing them to move faster.
 
• Unlike the incorrect statements in the question, particles are **neither stationary**, nor do they move only in gases. Their motion is a fundamental characteristic of all matter. *Hence, the correct answer is option 3.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **States of Matter:**

 
 
• **Solids:** Particles are closely packed and exhibit minimal movement, primarily vibrating in fixed positions.
 
• **Liquids:** Particles are less tightly packed compared to solids and can move past each other, giving liquids their fluidity.
 
• **Gases:** Particles are widely spaced and move freely and rapidly, exhibiting the highest kinetic energy among the three states.
 
 
 
• **Brownian Motion:**
 
 
• First observed by **Robert Brown** in **1827**, it refers to the random movement of microscopic particles suspended in a fluid.
 
• This phenomenon is caused by collisions between the suspended particles and the molecules of the fluid.
 
 
 
• **Temperature and Particle Movement:**
 
 
• Higher temperature leads to increased kinetic energy, causing particles to move faster.
 
• This principle is the basis for phenomena like diffusion, where particles spread from areas of higher concentration to lower concentration.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Statements Explained:**
 
 
• **"Particles of matter are too heavy to move":** Incorrect, as mass does not prevent motion; even heavier particles exhibit movement due to kinetic energy.
 
• **"Particles of matter are stationary unless force is applied":** Incorrect, as particles naturally move due to their kinetic energy, without external forces.
 
• **"Particles of matter move only in gases and not in solids or liquids":** Incorrect, as particle movement occurs in all states of matter, though the degree of movement varies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Diffusion:** This is the process by which particles spread from a region of higher concentration to lower concentration due to their motion. Examples include the mixing of gases or the dissolution of substances in liquids.
 
• **Intermolecular Forces:** The movement of particles in solids is restricted by strong intermolecular forces, whereas in gases, these forces are negligible, enabling rapid motion.
 
• **Applications:** Understanding particle movement is crucial in fields like **thermodynamics**, **chemical reactions**, and **material science**, where particle interactions determine outcomes.
 
• **Observation:** The kinetic energy and movement of particles can be indirectly observed in everyday phenomena like evaporation, boiling, and diffusion.

questions.question: Which of the following metals is most likely to be found in the free state in nature due to its low reactivity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gold**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gold** is one of the **least reactive metals**, which means it does not easily form compounds with other elements. This property allows gold to exist in its free state in nature.
 
• Gold has very low reactivity because it is placed at the bottom of the **reactivity series of metals**. It does not react with oxygen, water, or acids under standard conditions.
 
• Due to its inert nature, gold is found in nature primarily as **native gold**, often mixed with quartz or other minerals, rather than as compounds.
 
• Other metals such as **iron, zinc, and copper** are more reactive compared to gold. These metals are typically found as ores combined with oxygen, sulfur, or other elements.
 
• Gold’s unique chemical properties make it highly valuable and desirable for applications such as **jewelry, electronics, and investment** purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Iron:**

 
 
• Iron is a highly reactive metal and is usually found in nature as iron ores such as **hematite** (Fe₂O₃) and **magnetite** (Fe₃O₄).
 
• It reacts with oxygen and water, forming **iron oxides** such as rust under normal conditions.
 
• Iron is primarily used in construction, machinery, and as a key component in **steel production**.
 
 
 
• **Zinc:**
 
 
• Zinc is moderately reactive and is usually found as zinc ores like **zinc blende** (ZnS) or **calamine** (ZnCO₃).
 
• It reacts with acids and alkalis, releasing hydrogen gas.
 
• Zinc is widely used in galvanization, batteries, and alloys such as **brass**.
 
 
 
• **Copper:**
 
 
• Copper is less reactive than iron and zinc but more reactive than gold. It is often found as **malachite** (CuCO₃.Cu(OH)₂) and other ores.
 
• Copper reacts with oxygen at high temperatures, forming copper oxide.
 
• Due to its excellent electrical conductivity, copper is widely used in **electrical wiring** and electronics.
 
 
 
• **Gold:**
 
 
• Gold is found in nature in its native form as nuggets or grains in rocks and alluvial deposits.
 
• It does not corrode or tarnish even after prolonged exposure to air and water.
 
• Gold’s rarity and inertness make it a preferred choice for **jewelry, currency reserves, and electronics.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reactivity Series:**

 
 
• The **reactivity series** ranks metals based on their reactivity with water, acids, and oxygen.
 
• Gold is at the bottom of the series, indicating its **low reactivity**. Metals like potassium, sodium, and calcium are at the top, showing high reactivity.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Gold:**
 
 
• Gold is used in **electronics** due to its excellent conductivity and resistance to corrosion.
 
• It serves as a reliable investment option and is stored in the form of **bullion** or coins.
 
• Gold is widely used in **dentistry** and medicine for its biocompatibility.
 
 
 
• **Extraction of Gold:**
 
 
• Gold is extracted using methods such as **panning, sluicing, and cyanidation**.
 
• Cyanidation involves dissolving gold in a cyanide solution to separate it from impurities.

questions.question: Which of the following features is seen in every cell under a microscope?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cell membrane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **cell membrane**, also known as the plasma membrane, is a structure that surrounds all cells, providing them with a defined boundary and protecting the internal components from the external environment. This membrane is universally present in every type of cell, whether prokaryotic or eukaryotic.
 
• The cell membrane is primarily composed of a **phospholipid bilayer** along with embedded proteins, which allow selective transport of substances in and out of the cell. This selective permeability is critical for maintaining homeostasis.
 
• The **fluid mosaic model** describes the cell membrane as a dynamic structure where phospholipids and proteins can move laterally within the layer, ensuring flexibility and functionality.
 
• Other structures like lysosomes, mitochondria, and chromosomes are specific to certain cell types or stages of the cell cycle, but the cell membrane is a universal feature of all living cells.
 
• Its functions include providing structural support, facilitating communication between cells, and acting as a barrier against harmful substances. **Hence, the correct answer is the cell membrane.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lysosome:**

 
 
• Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles found in eukaryotic cells that contain hydrolytic enzymes. These enzymes help in the degradation of cellular waste and foreign particles.
 
• They are referred to as the "suicidal bags" of the cell because their rupture can lead to cell death.
 
• However, lysosomes are not present in all cells. For instance, they are absent in prokaryotic cells.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria:**
 
 
• Mitochondria are double-membrane-bound organelles found in most eukaryotic cells and are known as the "powerhouse of the cell" because they generate ATP through cellular respiration.
 
• They contain their own DNA and ribosomes, allowing them to produce some of their own proteins.
 
• Mitochondria are absent in prokaryotic cells, which instead rely on the cell membrane for energy production.
 
 
 
• **Chromosome:**
 
 
• Chromosomes are structures composed of DNA and proteins that carry genetic information. They are present in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells and in the nucleoid region of prokaryotic cells.
 
• However, chromosomes are not always visible under a microscope. They become distinctly visible only during cell division when they condense.
 
• In contrast, the cell membrane is consistently visible in all cells under a microscope.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Cell Membrane:**
 
 
• The cell membrane acts as a **protective barrier** for the cell, shielding it from environmental changes.
 
• It plays a critical role in **cell signaling**, allowing cells to communicate with each other through receptor proteins.
 
• The membrane's **selective permeability** ensures that essential nutrients enter the cell while waste products are expelled.
 
• It provides **mechanical support** and helps maintain the shape of the cell.

questions.question: Which substances are selectively reabsorbed in the nephron?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Glucose, amino acids, and water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **nephron** is the functional unit of the kidney responsible for filtering blood and forming urine. Selective reabsorption occurs in the nephron to ensure essential substances are retained in the body.
 
• **Glucose**: Almost all glucose is reabsorbed in the proximal convoluted tubule of the nephron through active transport. This ensures glucose, a vital energy source, is not lost in urine.
 
• **Amino acids**: Similar to glucose, amino acids are also actively reabsorbed in the proximal convoluted tubule. These are essential building blocks of proteins and must be preserved for bodily functions.
 
• **Water**: Water reabsorption occurs throughout the nephron but primarily in the proximal tubule, loop of Henle, distal tubule, and collecting duct. This process is regulated by hormones like ADH (antidiuretic hormone) to maintain fluid balance in the body.
 
• The process of selective reabsorption ensures that waste products like urea and excess ions are excreted while essential substances like glucose, amino acids, and water are conserved.
 
• The correct answer highlights the substances crucial for maintaining homeostasis in the body through selective reabsorption in the nephron.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Urea and Carbon Dioxide**:

 
 
• **Urea**: It is a waste product formed in the liver during protein metabolism. Urea is not reabsorbed selectively; it is excreted in the urine.
 
• **Carbon dioxide**: This is a gaseous waste product expelled through the lungs and not filtered or reabsorbed in the nephron.
 
 
 
• **Bile and Hydrochloric Acid**:
 
 
• **Bile**: Produced by the liver and stored in the gallbladder, bile aids in digestion. It is not filtered by the kidneys or reabsorbed in the nephron.
 
• **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)**: Found in the stomach, HCl aids in digestion and is unrelated to kidney function.
 
 
 
• **Platelets and Enzymes**:
 
 
• **Platelets**: These are cellular components of blood involved in clotting and are too large to be filtered by the nephron.
 
• **Enzymes**: These are proteins that catalyze biochemical reactions. They are not filtered or reabsorbed in the nephron under normal conditions.
 
 
 
• **Other Key Functions of the Nephron**:
 
 
• The nephron regulates **salt and ion balance** through reabsorption of sodium, potassium, and chloride ions.
 
• It helps maintain **acid-base balance** by reabsorbing bicarbonate and secreting hydrogen ions.
 
• The kidneys also play a role in producing hormones like **erythropoietin** (stimulates red blood cell production) and **renin** (regulates blood pressure).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT)**: Reabsorbs 65-70% of filtered water, all glucose, and most amino acids and ions.
 
• **Loop of Henle**: Responsible for concentrating urine by creating a gradient for water and salt reabsorption.
 
• **Distal Convoluted Tubule (DCT)**: Fine-tunes ion and pH balance through selective ion exchange.
 
• **Collecting Duct**: Final site for water reabsorption, regulated by ADH, determining urine concentration.

questions.question: A cyclist performing uniform circular motion throws an apple in his direction, the apple moves in a ____________.

options.text: straight line path opposite to the cyclist
circular path opposite to the cyclist
tangential path to the circular path at that point

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**tangential path to the circular path at that point**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uniform Circular Motion:** When a cyclist is in uniform circular motion, they are moving along a circular path with a constant speed. The velocity of the cyclist is always tangential to the circular path at every point, and the centripetal force acts towards the center of the circle to maintain the circular motion.
 
• **Projectile Thrown by the Cyclist:** When the cyclist throws an apple in their direction, the apple initially possesses two components of velocity:
 
 
• A tangential velocity component due to the cyclist's motion along the circular path at that instant.
 
• An additional velocity imparted by the action of throwing the apple.
 
 
 
• **Resultant Path of the Apple:** According to Newton's first law of motion (the law of inertia), the apple will continue to move in the direction of the tangential velocity component at the point of release. Therefore, the apple follows a **tangential path to the circular motion of the cyclist at that point**.
 
• **Why Not a Circular Path?** The apple does not follow a circular path because, after being thrown, it is no longer under the influence of the centripetal force that keeps the cyclist in circular motion. Instead, it moves freely under the influence of its inertia and external forces such as gravity.
 
• **Correct Answer:** Hence, the correct explanation for the motion of the apple is that it follows a **tangential path to the circular path at that point**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion (Law of Inertia):** An object will continue in its state of rest or uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force. In this scenario, after the apple is released, it is no longer influenced by the centripetal force, and thus it moves in the direction of its initial velocity.
 
• **Tangential Velocity:** The velocity of an object in circular motion is always directed tangentially to the circular path. At the point of release, the apple carries this tangential velocity, leading to its motion along a straight tangential path.
 
• **Circular Motion Dynamics:** Circular motion is maintained by a centripetal force that acts towards the center of the circle. This force is essential for keeping an object in a circular trajectory. Once the apple is released, it is no longer subject to this force, and hence it does not follow a circular path.
 
• **Gravity's Role:** If we consider gravity, the apple will eventually follow a parabolic trajectory due to the combined effect of its horizontal tangential velocity and the downward gravitational force. However, the initial direction of motion remains tangential.
 
• **Applications:** Understanding the tangential motion of an object in circular motion is crucial in various fields, such as satellite launching, amusement park rides (e.g., roller coasters), and vehicle dynamics while turning on curved roads.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option Analysis:**

 
 
• **Option 1:** "Straight line path opposite to the cyclist" is incorrect because the apple is not influenced by a force to reverse its motion.
 
• **Option 2:** "Circular path opposite to the cyclist" is incorrect as the apple is no longer under the influence of centripetal force.
 
• **Option 3:** "Tangential path to the circular path at that point" is correct as explained above.
 
• **Option 4:** "Circular path as the cyclist" is incorrect because the apple does not stay in circular motion after being released.
 
 
 
• **Real-life Examples:**
 
 
• When a stone tied to a string is whirled in a circle and the string breaks, the stone moves tangentially to the circle.
 
• Water droplets flung off a spinning wheel follow a tangential path.

questions.question: The potential energy of a body depends on which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both mass and height**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potential energy** is the energy possessed by a body due to its position or configuration. It is expressed mathematically as **PE = mgh**, where:

 
 
• **m** is the mass of the object (in kilograms).
 
• **g** is the acceleration due to gravity (approximately **9.8 m/s²** on Earth).
 
• **h** is the height of the object above the reference point (in meters).
 
 
 
• The formula clearly shows that **potential energy depends on both the mass (m) and the height (h)** of the object. Hence, the correct option is **Both mass and height**__.
 
• **Height:** The higher the object is above the reference point, the greater its potential energy. This is because the object has more energy stored due to its elevated position.
 
• **Mass:** The greater the mass of the object, the more potential energy it possesses for the same height, as energy is directly proportional to mass.
 
• Other factors like **speed** or kinetic energy do not influence potential energy. They are associated with the energy of motion, not position.
 
• Similarly, considering only **mass** or **height** individually is incorrect, as both parameters are crucial for determining potential energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gravitational Potential Energy:**

 
 
• This type of potential energy is due to the gravitational force acting on an object.
 
• It is stored in an object as a result of its vertical position or height relative to a lower reference point.
 
• Example: A book placed on a table possesses gravitational potential energy, which will be converted into kinetic energy if it falls.
 
 
 
• **Elastic Potential Energy:**
 
 
• It is stored in elastic materials like springs, rubber bands, or any object that can stretch or compress.
 
• Example: A compressed spring stores elastic potential energy, which is released when the spring is allowed to expand.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Energy vs. Potential Energy:**
 
 
• **Kinetic energy** is the energy of motion, while **potential energy** is the energy of position or configuration.
 
• The total mechanical energy of an object is the sum of its kinetic and potential energy.
 
• Example: When an object falls, its potential energy decreases, while its kinetic energy increases, keeping the total energy constant (law of conservation of energy).
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Potential Energy:**
 
 
• **Mass:** Heavier objects have greater potential energy for the same height.
 
• **Height:** Objects placed higher above the ground have more potential energy.
 
• **Gravitational Force:** The value of gravitational acceleration (g) can vary slightly depending on location (e.g., Earth's poles vs. equator).
 
 
 
• **Applications of Potential Energy:**
 
 
• It is utilized in hydroelectric power plants, where water stored at a height is used to generate electricity.
 
• In archery, the stretched bow stores elastic potential energy, which is transferred to the arrow as kinetic energy.
 
• Roller coasters rely on potential energy at the highest points, which is converted into kinetic energy during the descent.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Unit of Potential Energy:** The SI unit of potential energy is the **joule (J)**, where 1 joule = 1 kg·m²/s².
 
• **Conservation of Energy:** Energy is neither created nor destroyed. The potential energy of an object is converted to other forms of energy, such as kinetic energy, during motion.
 
• **Real-life Example:** Water stored in a dam at a height has potential energy, which is used to rotate turbines for electricity generation when released.
 
• **Variation in Gravitational Acceleration:** The value of **g (9.8 m/s²)** slightly varies depending on altitude and latitude.

questions.question: Which of the following is secreted directly into the blood and carried to different parts of the body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Adrenaline**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Adrenaline** is a hormone secreted by the adrenal glands directly into the bloodstream.
 
• It is commonly known as the "fight or flight" hormone because it helps the body respond to stressful situations.
 
• Adrenaline increases the heart rate, expands air passages in the lungs, dilates the pupils, and redirects blood flow to muscles, preparing the body for immediate action.
 
• This hormone plays a critical role in regulating metabolic processes and maintaining homeostasis during emergencies.
 
• Unlike other substances like pancreatic juice, bile juice, or saliva, which are secreted into ducts, adrenaline is released directly into the bloodstream.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pancreatic Juice:**

 
 
• Pancreatic juice contains digestive enzymes such as amylase, lipase, and protease.
 
• It is secreted by the pancreas into the small intestine through the pancreatic duct.
 
• This juice helps in the digestion of carbohydrates, fats, and proteins in the duodenum.
 
• Unlike adrenaline, it is not secreted directly into the bloodstream but into the digestive tract.
 
 
 
• **Bile Juice:**
 
 
• Bile juice is produced by the liver and stored in the gallbladder.
 
• It is secreted into the small intestine through the bile duct and helps in emulsifying fats for digestion.
 
• Bile juice contains bile salts, bile pigments, and cholesterol but is not released into the bloodstream.
 
 
 
• **Saliva:**
 
 
• Saliva is secreted by salivary glands into the mouth.
 
• It contains enzymes like salivary amylase, which begin the digestion of starch.
 
• Saliva is involved in the process of chewing and swallowing but is not released into the bloodstream.
 
 
 
• **Adrenal Glands:**
 
 
• Adrenal glands are small triangular glands located on top of the kidneys.
 
• They produce hormones like adrenaline, noradrenaline, cortisol, and aldosterone.
 
• Adrenaline and noradrenaline are secreted directly into the bloodstream to regulate stress responses.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Functions of Adrenaline:**

 
 
• Adrenaline helps in increasing blood sugar levels by stimulating glycogen breakdown in the liver.
 
• It enhances oxygen supply to the brain and muscles during stressful situations.
 
• It suppresses non-essential functions like digestion during emergencies to conserve energy.
 
 
 
• **Medical Applications:**
 
 
• Adrenaline is used in emergency medicine to treat severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis).
 
• It is also used in certain cardiac conditions to stimulate the heart during a cardiac arrest.

questions.question: At maturity, an organism breaks into smaller pieces, which grow into new individuals. What is this process called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fragmentation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fragmentation** is a form of asexual reproduction where an organism breaks into smaller pieces or fragments, and each fragment grows into a new, complete individual.
 
• This process is common in simple multicellular organisms such as **sponges, flatworms, algae, and fungi**.
 
• Fragmentation allows for rapid population growth in favorable environmental conditions as it does not require the fusion of gametes or a mate.
 
• The new individuals formed are genetically identical to the parent organism because there is no genetic recombination involved in this process.
 
• Examples include **hydra** (a type of coelenterate), **planaria** (a flatworm), and certain types of algae like **Spirogyra**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fusion:**

 
 
• **Fusion** is a process in sexual reproduction where two gametes (male and female) fuse to form a zygote, which develops into a new organism.
 
• This process occurs in both plants and animals and involves genetic recombination, leading to genetic diversity.
 
• Examples: Fertilization in humans and flowering plants.
 
 
 
• **Budding:**
 
 
• **Budding** is another form of asexual reproduction in which a new organism develops as an outgrowth or bud from the parent organism.
 
• The bud remains attached to the parent for some time before detaching and becoming an independent organism.
 
• Examples include **yeast** and **hydra**.
 
 
 
• **Fission:**
 
 
• **Fission** refers to the division of a single organism into two or more individuals of equal size, typically seen in unicellular organisms.
 
• It can be of two types: **binary fission** (splitting into two) and **multiple fission** (splitting into many).
 
• Examples include **amoeba** and **paramecium**.
 
 
 
• **Other Characteristics of Fragmentation:**
 
 
• It is an efficient mode of reproduction in non-motile organisms as it does not require movement to find a mate.
 
• Fragmentation often occurs in aquatic environments where water currents assist in the distribution of fragments.
 
• Organisms that reproduce via fragmentation can regenerate lost parts, a feature critical to this type of reproduction.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Advantages of Fragmentation:**

 
 
• It is a quick method of reproduction that helps in rapid population increase.
 
• It ensures the survival of species in a stable and favorable environment.
 
• The absence of genetic variation ensures that all offspring are well-suited to the current environment.
 
 
 
• **Disadvantages of Fragmentation:**
 
 
• Lack of genetic variation makes the population vulnerable to changes in the environment, diseases, and predators.
 
• Overpopulation due to rapid reproduction can lead to resource depletion in the habitat.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of cross-pollination over self-pollination?

options.text: Produces progeny that is identical to parent
Does not depend on pollinating agents for producing progeny
Introduces genetic variations, which improves chances of survival in progeny
Requires less energy input for generating the progeny

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Introduces genetic variations, which improves chances of survival in progeny**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cross-pollination** refers to the transfer of pollen from the anther of one flower to the stigma of a flower on a different plant of the same species. This process relies on external agents such as wind, water, or animals.
 
• **Genetic variations:** Cross-pollination introduces genetic diversity in the progeny by combining genetic material from two different plants. This increases the chances of survival and adaptability to environmental changes and disease resistance.
 
• **Improved adaptability:** The genetic variation introduced through cross-pollination enables the progeny to adapt better to changing environmental conditions, such as temperature fluctuations, soil differences, and pest attacks.
 
• **Evolutionary advantages:** Cross-pollination promotes evolution by increasing the genetic pool, which can lead to the emergence of new traits that may provide a competitive advantage to the species over time.
 
• **Avoids inbreeding depression:** Unlike self-pollination, cross-pollination prevents inbreeding depression, which can result in reduced vigor, fertility, and overall health of the progeny due to a lack of genetic diversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Self-pollination:**

 
 
• Self-pollination involves the transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma of the same flower or another flower on the same plant.
 
• It leads to the production of progeny that are genetically identical to the parent, resulting in limited genetic variation.
 
• While it is an energy-efficient process and does not require pollinators, it can result in inbreeding depression, reducing the plant's adaptability and vigor.
 
 
 
• **Pollinating agents:**
 
 
• Cross-pollination depends on external agents such as insects (bees, butterflies), wind, water, and animals for the transfer of pollen.
 
• For example, plants with brightly colored flowers attract insects as pollinators, while wind-pollinated plants, like wheat and maize, produce lightweight pollen grains for easy dispersal.
 
 
 
• **Examples of cross-pollinated plants:**
 
 
• Crops such as **apple, cucumber, sunflower, and mustard** rely on cross-pollination for better yield and genetic diversity.
 
• In horticulture, cross-pollination is often used to create hybrid plants with desirable traits such as higher yield, disease resistance, or improved flavor.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of self- and cross-pollination:**
 
 
• Self-pollination is more energy-efficient but lacks genetic diversity.
 
• Cross-pollination, while more energy-intensive and dependent on external agents, ensures genetic variation, adaptability, and resilience in plants.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Energy input:** Cross-pollination requires more energy investment in producing attractive flowers, nectar, or lightweight pollen grains to facilitate pollination through external agents.
 
• **Dependency on agents:** While cross-pollination has numerous benefits, its reliance on pollinators can make plants vulnerable to environmental factors affecting pollinator populations, such as habitat loss or climate change.
 
• **Hybrid vigor (Heterosis):** Cross-pollination often results in hybrid offspring that exhibit heterosis, characterized by superior qualities such as increased growth, yield, or resistance to diseases compared to their parents.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Loudness depends on frequency**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Loudness depends on frequency**: This statement is incorrect__. Loudness primarily depends on the **amplitude** of the sound wave and not on its frequency. While frequency determines the pitch of the sound, the amplitude determines how loud or soft a sound is perceived.
 
• **Loud sound has large amplitude**: This statement is __correct__. A sound wave with a large amplitude corresponds to a loud sound. Amplitude is directly related to the energy of the wave, making the sound more intense.
 
• **Soft sound has small amplitude**: This statement is __correct__. A sound wave with a small amplitude is perceived as a soft sound because it has lower energy compared to a wave with a higher amplitude.
 
• **Loudness depends on amplitude**: This statement is __correct__. Loudness is directly proportional to the amplitude of the sound wave. Larger amplitudes result in louder sounds, and smaller amplitudes result in softer sounds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Amplitude and Loudness:**

 
 
• The **amplitude** of a sound wave represents the maximum displacement of particles in the medium through which the sound travels.
 
• **Louder sounds** have larger amplitudes because they carry more energy.
 
• For example, a whisper has a small amplitude, while a shout has a large amplitude.
 
 
 
• **Frequency and Pitch:**
 
 
• The **frequency** of a sound wave determines its **pitch**, not its loudness.
 
• Higher frequencies produce higher-pitched sounds (e.g., a bird's chirping), while lower frequencies produce lower-pitched sounds (e.g., a drumbeat).
 
• Frequency is measured in **Hertz (Hz)**.
 
 
 
• **Loudness Measurement:**
 
 
• Loudness is measured in **decibels (dB)**, a logarithmic unit that quantifies the intensity of a sound.
 
• Sounds above **85 dB** can cause hearing damage with prolonged exposure.
 
 
 
• **Human Hearing Range:**
 
 
• The average human ear can hear sounds in the frequency range of **20 Hz to 20,000 Hz**.
 
• The sensitivity of the ear to different frequencies varies; humans are most sensitive to frequencies around **1,000–5,000 Hz**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sound Wave Characteristics:**

 
 
• Sound waves are **longitudinal waves**, meaning particles in the medium vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation.
 
• The three main characteristics of sound waves are **amplitude**, **frequency**, and **wavelength**.
 
 
 
• **Threshold of Hearing:**
 
 
• The **threshold of hearing** is the minimum intensity level of sound that the human ear can detect, approximately **0 dB**.
 
• Sounds exceeding **120 dB** are considered painful to human ears.
 
 
 
• **Resonance and Loudness:**
 
 
• **Resonance** occurs when a sound wave matches the natural frequency of an object, amplifying its loudness.
 
• This principle is used in musical instruments to enhance sound output.

questions.question: When the current in a circuit is doubled, keeping resistance constant, the power dissipated in the resistor becomes:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Four times**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The power dissipated in a resistor is calculated using the formula **P = I²R**, where **P** is the power, **I** is the current, and **R** is the resistance.
 
• If the current in the circuit is doubled, the new current becomes **2I**. Substituting this into the formula: **P = (2I)²R = 4I²R**.
 
• This shows that the power dissipated becomes **four times** the original power when the current is doubled while keeping the resistance constant.
 
• This relationship arises because power is proportional to the square of the current. Therefore, any change in current has a squared effect on the power.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is that the power dissipated in the resistor becomes **four times**.&l
